title: One coffee, please
title_target: ერთი ყავა, თუ შეიძლება — Erti q'ava, tu sheidzleba
goal: Order drinks and food at a café, say what you want, and tackle the sound ყ for the first time — in a word you'll say every morning.
bekal: order with the pattern ერთი … თუ შეიძლება
say მინდა (I want) and არ მინდა (I don't want)
ask whether something is available: … გაქვთ?
ask for the bill and pay
pronounce ყავა with the right ყ sound

dialogs.title: დიალოგი — At a café near Rustaveli
dialogs.intro: Ani walks into a small café and orders breakfast. The server, Sopo, talks fast like servers everywhere — notice how Ani uses the same single pattern for everything she orders.

notes: **ერთი … თუ შეიძლება is the only pattern you need to order anything.** Number + item + "if possible". *ერთი ჩაი, თუ შეიძლება* (one tea), *ორი ყავა, თუ შეიძლება* (two coffees). The noun stays in its dictionary form, completely unchanged.

**თუ შეიძლება goes at the END of the sentence.** ⚠️ Learners sometimes put it first, copying "please, one coffee". The natural Georgian is *ერთი ყავა, თუ შეიძლება* — the request first, the politeness after.

**მინდა means "I want", and it doesn't take the ვ- prefix.** It's one of the inverted verbs you met in unit 4: მინდა (I want), გინდა (you want), უნდა (he/she wants). The negative is *არ მინდა* — the most useful refusal in Georgia, because people will keep offering you food.

**რძით means "with milk" — one word, not two.** The ending **-ით** means "with / using", replacing the English preposition entirely. რძე (milk) → რძ**ით**, კვერცხი (egg) → კვერცხ**ით**, შაქარი (sugar) → შაქრ**ით**. Unit 13 uses it for transport: ავტობუს**ით** (by bus).

**გაქვთ? = "do you (pl.) have?" — this is how you ask whether something is available.** Not "is there?" but "do you have?". *ჩაი გაქვთ?* (do you have tea?), *წყალი გაქვთ?* (do you have water?). The answer is *კი, გვაქვს* (yes, we have) or *არა, არ გვაქვს*.
**რამდენი ღირს? = how much is it.** ღირს means "costs, is worth", and it doesn't change for one item or several. The next unit fills the remaining gap: the numbers.

**ხაჭაპური comes in more than twenty varieties, and every region defends its own.** The two most common: **იმერული** (round, cheese inside) and **აჭარული** (boat-shaped, with a runny egg and butter in the middle). Asking *რა განსხვავებაა?* in any café will make the server happy to explain.

grammars.title: მინდა — the verb "want" and its relatives
body: This group is small, used constantly, and all of them work in reverse: the grammatical subject is **the thing**, while the person comes in as a prefix.
after: *ყავა მინდა* literally means "coffee is-wanted-by-me". That's why the verb has no ვ- prefix.
⚠️ **უნდა has two jobs.** Besides "he/she wants", it also means "must" when it stands before another verb: *უნდა წავიდე* (I must go). Only what follows tells them apart.

grammars.title: The ending -ით: with, using, by
body: One ending that does the job of three English prepositions.
after: The opposite is **-ის გარეშე** (without) or the frame **უ-…-ოდ**: *შაქრის გარეშე* / *უშაქროდ* — without sugar. The first is easier and always safe.

sections.title: The drinks list, and how to pay

blocks.title: Six sentences for a whole café visit
items: **ერთი ყავა, თუ შეიძლება.** — One coffee, please.
**მენიუ გაქვთ?** (meniu gakvt) — Do you have a menu?
**ეს რა არის?** — What's this? (pointing at the menu — the sentence from unit 2 again)
**ბარათით შეიძლება?** (baratit sheidzleba) — Can I pay by card?

blocks.text: Back to the sound **ყ** once more, because it's in a word you'll say every morning. ყავა isn't "kava" and isn't "khava": close your throat at the very back of the tongue, then release it short. If you miss, you'll still get your coffee — but spend thirty seconds saying ყავა, ყველი, წყალი out loud now, before the wrong sound becomes a habit.

One thing that often surprises people: in many small Tbilisi cafés you pay **after** eating, at the counter rather than at the table, and nobody will come to collect. If you've finished and no one comes over, stand up and say *ანგარიში, თუ შეიძლება* toward the counter. A 10% tip is appreciated but not required; many places already add it as *მომსახურება* (momsakhureba, service charge) on the bill.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: თუ შეიძლება — გაქვთ — არ მინდა — ღირს — ანგარიში
ერთი ყავა, თუ შეიძლება. — ხაჭაპური გაქვთ? — შაქარი არ მინდა. — რამდენი ღირს? — ძალიან გემრიელია.
ერთი ჩაი, თუ შეიძლება. — წყალი გაქვთ? — ყავა რძით მინდა. — შაქარი არ მინდა. — რამდენი ღირს? — ანგარიში, თუ შეიძლება.
